- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (especially >79.00), leading to overcorrection; apply dampening factor to subsequent days.
- Forecast bias toward higher prices persists when sentiment is mixed or trending upward; consider smoothing or lagged mean adjustment.
- In early horizon (e.g., 30d) forecasts, model often fails to capture sharp downward moves after strong positive sentiment; add buffer for volatility decay.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals, model should not overreact to single-day spikes; apply decay-weighted sentiment smoothing.
